findings.title: The schema's 'Not tied to the murder: N' button in the trial console does nothing
findings.surface: the case schema in the console's slot
findings.what_happens: The console's schema is drawn folded (case-trial.mjs:56, fold: true), and with evidence not tied to the murder the Map's builder draws a button data-drpg-case-fold, aria-expanded=false, under the graph (case-map.mjs:223-224). The console wires the graph with wireCaseMap(region, { camera }) alone, so the click runs onFold's default, an empty function. Nothing unfolds and nothing is said; the folded Remnants, and a 'presented' mark on one of them, cannot be seen in the console.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM running a trial presses 'Not tied to the murder: 3' under the schema and nothing happens.
findings.expected: The press unfolds the rest of the evidence, as on the Investigation's Map (investigation.mjs:1860), or the console draws the line as text, not as a button.
findings.refutation_tried: git grep data-drpg-case-fold and onFold in scripts/: one listener (case-map.mjs:495) and one caller that hands an onFold (investigation.mjs:1860); case-trial.mjs hands none. The source's own note (case-map.mjs:222, commit 9c1a4104) says the press folds nothing there and names no decision of the owner. styles/*.css: no rule hides .drpg-case-fold or .drpg-case-gap in .drpg-window-trial. Tier 0 reads the button's aria-expanded; no test or scenario presses it in the console.
findings.probe: game.drpg.manageClassTrial() in a chapter whose case holds a Remnant not tied to the murder; press `.drpg-window-trial [data-drpg-trial-schema] [data-drpg-case-fold]`; compare aria-expanded and the count of `button[data-drpg-node]` before and after.

findings.title: Your turn: Keep speaking, the X and Escape take Done and Pass away for the rest of the turn
findings.what_happens: promptTurn marks the turn as asked before its window opens and draws the window once for a turn. Keep speaking is the primary, so Enter and Space press it; it, the header's X and Escape close the window and the function returns before any request. The clock asks promptTurn again every second and it returns at line 175 for the same turn, so Done and Pass are not drawn again until the next turn; only the thesis road puts the mark back (lines 210-215). The window's own words are 'Press Done when you finish, or Pass to give up your turn', and no other control of the module asks trial.turn for Done or Pass.
findings.failure_scenario: The Closing Argument's speaker presses Enter on the prompt at the start of 300 s, finishes after two minutes and has no Done to press; the stretch runs until its clock or the GM's Skip.
findings.expected: Done and Pass stay within reach for as long as the turn is the speaker's, or the window says that closing it ends the choice. The handbooks name Done and Pass alone and not Keep speaking (player-handbook.en.md:894, gm-handbook.en.md:1553).
findings.refutation_tried: The note at trial-prompt.mjs:194-197 (E70 fix p2-G3) makes Keep speaking the default on purpose, so Enter ends no turn, and says the GM's bar still skips the turn; it does not say Done should be out of reach after it. git grep promptedFor: put back to null only at :214. git grep requestTurn and DRPG.Trial.turn: trial-prompt.mjs alone; hud.mjs draws no Done or Pass. Test R1365 reads the footer's order only.
findings.probe: As a player whose student speaks in a Testimony, press `.drpg-your-turn button[data-action="keep"]`; three seconds later `.drpg-your-turn` is absent while `game.settings.get('danganronpa-rpg','trialQueue').round.step` is unchanged.

findings.title: The Closing Argument's buttons refuse with 'The Closing Argument did not change.' and never the reason written for it
findings.surface: the Class Trial console; the Closing's pick window
findings.control: Confirm the speaker; {name} ({m:ss}); Resume the Closing Argument; Pick a speaker (the pick window)
findings.what_happens: The row's buttons run through runClosingOp, which asks nothing before the press (the bar's runBarOp asks barRefusal and says its key). closingCall runs the floor's op, and on the primary closingStepInStep is called without `why`, so a refusal of the machine comes back as null and the GM reads DRPG.Floor.closing.notDone. The machine's reasons - closing.absent 'That player is not connected: pick someone else.', noDrawn, noChoice, notParticipant, noDecision, notInExchange, voteOpen, nothingToResume - stand in both language files and no road of the module shows them.
findings.failure_scenario: The drawn volunteer's player drops out; the console still offers Confirm the speaker, and each press says only 'The Closing Argument did not change.'
findings.expected: The reason the machine gives, as a greyed bar button says its own; here, that the player is not connected and somebody else is to be picked.
findings.refutation_tried: git grep of each key (closing.absent, noDrawn, noChoice, notParticipant, noDecision, notInExchange, voteOpen, nothingToResume) in scripts/: floor-machine.mjs returns them and nothing localizes them. `why: true` has one caller, a volunteer's claim (trial-modes.mjs:336), mapped to the bridge's words. On a GM who is not the primary the request trial.gm answers a floor or null the same way (bridge-asks.mjs:339-348, trial-floor.mjs:736-742). R1048 reads the row's markup, not a refusal.
findings.probe: In a Closing whose floor says closing.choice 'confirm', with the drawn student's player disconnected, press `.drpg-window-trial [data-drpg-bar="closing"][data-drpg-closing="confirm"]` and read the toast.

findings.title: 'Your turn' and 'I'll sum up' do not open on the floor's first write in a world: createSetting is not heard
findings.surface: the speaker's prompt; the volunteers' question
findings.what_happens: A participant's clock, which opens both prompts and calls a turn over, is started by renderTrialPrompt, and that runs at ready and on the hook updateSetting for the floor's key. The module's own notes say a world setting's first write makes its document and is createSetting in Foundry (gm-store.mjs:1750-1753, trial-scene.mjs:1714-1715, where both hooks are heard). In a world whose floor was never written, a round, the Closing or a Scrum Debate started as the first mode is that write: no clock starts on the players' browsers, the first speaker gets no window with Done and Pass, and the Closing's volunteers are not asked, until the floor is written again.
findings.failure_scenario: A new world's first Class Trial: the GM starts the Closing Argument from discussion and no player is asked 'I'll sum up' in its 30 s.
findings.expected: Both hooks, as gm-store.mjs, trial-scene.mjs, fog.mjs and voice.mjs listen.
findings.refutation_tried: git grep renderTrialPrompt: its two callers are the ready hook and updateSetting; the setting's onChange (settings.mjs:2962-2967) goes to sync.mjs and does not call it. What is not established: Foundry's create on a first write is read from the module's notes, not from Foundry; the harness fires updateSetting for both (gm-store.mjs:1752), so no headless run shows it; and a world may hold the floor's document already (a season reset writes it empty, trial.mjs:766-768).
findings.probe: On Foundry v14, in a world where `game.settings.storage.get('world').getSetting('danganronpa-rpg.trialQueue')` is undefined, start a Testimony from discussion with a player connected: on the player's page `.drpg-your-turn` is absent through the first turn and present from the second.

findings.title: Start the Final Trial stays greyed after a Mastermind is picked while the console stands open
findings.what_happens: The button is disabled, with the title 'No Mastermind set. Pick one in Season setup first.', from view.mastermind, read off the GMs' store by mastermindActor at each redraw of the console. The pick writes that store alone (a client setting), and the console's live region watches the module's world settings, three hooks and two other stores; with no floor open no tick redraws it either. So the footer keeps the greyed button until some world setting of the module is written or the console is opened again.
findings.failure_scenario: With the console open and no trial running, a GM follows the button's hint, picks the Mastermind in Season setup and comes back to a button still greyed with the same hint.
findings.expected: The footer follows the pick, as it follows the register and the deaths (the two stores it does watch).
findings.refutation_tried: live.mjs listenFor (:304-352): updateSetting for the module's world keys, the named hooks and clientSettingChanged for the stores named only. git grep mastermindStore: no watch names it. The primary's clock beat is a GM store's too (hud-elapsed.mjs:153), so nothing periodic redraws a console with no floor. A redraw does put it right: liveFooter redraws the buttons in place.
findings.probe: With no Mastermind set, open the console; from the browser's console `await game.drpg.setMastermind(game.actors.contents.find(a => a.type === 'character'))`; read `.drpg-window-trial button[data-action="toggleFinal"]`.disabled a few seconds later.

findings.title: After a Reveal made in discussion, its row and 'Left to reveal' stay on the console
findings.control: Reveal (a row of Missing Key Remnants)
findings.what_happens: The list is drawn from missingKeys() and the reveal record, both read off the Key plan's store. A Reveal writes items, a token, GM stores and whispers (trial-modes.mjs:429-471, key-remnants.mjs:83); none of them is in the console's watch, and the one-second tick runs only while a floor is open. So in discussion the revealed row keeps its Reveal button and the count does not fall until something else redraws the region. A second press is answered ('That Key Remnant is not missing...'), so nothing is revealed twice.
findings.failure_scenario: With the debate closed, a GM reveals a Key Remnant; the row still stands with its button and 'Left to reveal: 2' still reads 2.
findings.expected: The list and the count follow the Reveal at once, as they do while a floor is open.
findings.refutation_tried: Read revealInStep and what it calls for a write the console hears (createTruthBullet, markKeyFound -> revealRemnantToFinder, recordKeyRevealed, whisperToOwner): items, a token update, GM stores and chat, none a world setting of the module as far as read; a write deeper in those calls was not excluded, which is why this is suspected. case-trial.mjs:126 does watch keyPlanStore, for the schema's region, not the console's.
findings.probe: In a running trial with no floor and a missing Key Remnant, press `.drpg-window-trial [data-drpg-reveal]`, confirm; read `.drpg-reveal-list li` and the 'Left to reveal' line two seconds later, with no other write in between.

findings.title: Re-point opens on the current target, and Re-point pressed on it is refused as 'You cannot do that right now.'
findings.what_happens: The window lists every participant but the objector and marks the Objection's present target as chosen, so the primary button and Enter ask for the target it already has. The primary's step turns that down with the key DRPG.Floor.repointSame and answers null; repointOnPrimary words every null as 'the student named may not be objected to now', which the bridge says as cannotNow. The texts 'The Objection is already aimed at that student.' and 'That student's player is not here to answer.' are in both language files and are shown on no road.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM presses Re-point on the bar and then Enter in the window: the toast reads that Re-point the Objection was not carried out and that they cannot do that right now.
findings.expected: The refusal's own words (already aimed at that student; that player is not here), or a window that leaves the current target out of its list.
findings.refutation_tried: bridge-guards.mjs:452 maps the text to cannotNow; sayNotDone (:581) says it on the primary's own road too (bridge-asks.mjs:325-333). git grep repointSame and repointAbsent: returned by trial-floor.mjs and floor-machine.mjs, localized nowhere outside the tests' key census. The tier 2 Re-point test names another target.
findings.probe: With an Objection running, `await game.drpg.manageClassTrial()`, press `[data-drpg-bar="repoint"]`, then the window's `button[data-action="repoint"]` without touching the select; read the toast and the floor's targetId.

findings.title: Finish the verdict is drawn, enabled, on a GM who is not the verdict's runner
findings.what_happens: While a verdict stands stopped the footer draws Finish the verdict on every GM's console. Only the verdict's runner may run it: on any other GM the press is always refused, with 'Only {name} can finish the verdict. Ask {name}.' The lead line of that console names the runner too, and the button is not the default there, so the refusal is told twice; the button itself still looks pressable.
findings.failure_scenario: A second GM sees Finish the verdict after a step failed, presses it and is told to ask the other GM.
findings.expected: On a GM who is not the runner the button is left out or greyed with the runner's name as its title, as Start the Final Trial carries its reason.
findings.refutation_tried: E10 fix r2-G2's notes (trial-floor-ui.mjs:800-805, verdict.mjs:1099-1104) decide who runs Finish and that the next step is no button on the other GMs; they do not say the button should stay drawn there. The press is told, so this is not silent.
findings.probe: Scenario 92's state (a verdict whose step failed) with two GMs: on the GM who did not give it, `.drpg-window-trial button[data-action="finishVerdict"]` is present and not disabled; press it and read the toast.

findings.title: A schema tile's start is greyed in a Nonstop Debate with 'Another mode is running. End it first.' while the mode picker starts the same mode
findings.surface: the case schema in the console's slot
findings.what_happens: The tile's start is disabled, with that title, whenever any floor is open (floorOpen is Boolean(trialFloor())). The console's own picker greys Testimony, Panic Round, the Closing and the zone modes only while a mode other than the debate holds the floor, and the primary's machine starts each of them over an open debate. So during a debate the tile says the debate must end first, and one region above it the same start works. The file's header still says 'the console offers no start then either' (case-trial.mjs:14-15), which was so before the picker.
findings.failure_scenario: In an open debate a GM points at a node's Testimony start, reads 'Another mode is running. End it first.', closes the debate for nothing, or finds the picker's Testimony pressable.
findings.expected: The tile's start greyed by the picker's rule and with its reason.
findings.refutation_tried: floor-machine.mjs:522 (a round), :259 (the Closing) and trial-zones.mjs:237 (the zone modes) refuse a start only when the floor's mode is not the debate. LIVE-E99-01 asks that the tile's start 'greys while another mode runs', which a debate is not held to elsewhere.
findings.probe: Open a debate, then in the console read `[data-drpg-case-start="startTestimony"]`.disabled and its title against `[data-drpg-mode-action="startTestimony"]`'s aria-disabled.

findings.title: In Straw Poll, Logic Dive and Scrum Debate OBJECTION! is held with the words of a running Objection
findings.surface: OBJECTION! on the trial bar and the voice tile
findings.what_happens: floorRefusal words a mode that allows no Objection in three ways: a round by its name ('Nobody can raise an Objection in {mode}.'), the Closing with nobody speaking, and everything else as an Objection already running. The three zone modes allow none (MODE_RULES object: false) and are neither, so the button's tooltip and its press say 'You cannot raise an Objection right now. While an Objection runs, you can raise one in the Rebuttal that follows it, at one of the two speaking in it.' No Objection runs, and no Rebuttal will follow.
findings.failure_scenario: A player in a Straw Poll hovers or presses OBJECTION! and is told to wait for a Rebuttal that is not coming.
findings.expected: The mode's own line, as a Panic Round has: nobody can raise an Objection in a Straw Poll.
findings.refutation_tried: floor-machine.mjs:51 isRoundMode covers Testimony and the Panic Round only; zone-machine.mjs:44 isZoneMode is a list of its own. hud.mjs:1551-1558 and :1572 show floorRefusal's text unchanged as the tooltip and the warning.
findings.probe: On a player's page during a Straw Poll: `(await import('/modules/danganronpa-rpg/scripts/trial.mjs')).objectionButtonState(game.user.character)` and read `.text`.

findings.title: The mode picker's greyed Nonstop Debate says 'The debate is already running.' in a round, the Closing and the zone modes
findings.what_happens: The picker's reason for the debate's start is asked before the busy line and is the same for every open floor. In Testimony, a Panic Round, the Closing Argument or a zone mode no debate is running, and the reason the machine holds for it is DRPG.Floor.startBusy ('A debate cannot open while a round, the Closing Argument, or a zone mode holds the floor. End that mode first.'). The button's title, and the warning a press on it gives, say the debate is already running.
findings.failure_scenario: In a Testimony started from discussion a GM presses the greyed Nonstop Debate and reads that the debate is already running.
findings.expected: The busy line for a floor that is not the debate's, the machine's startBusy.
findings.refutation_tried: floor-machine.mjs:505 gives startBusy for a start over a round, the Closing or a zone mode; trial-floor.mjs:884-888 says it on startFloor's road. In an Objection or its Rebuttal the debate's family does hold the floor, and the line is fair there.
findings.probe: Start a Testimony from discussion, then read the title of `.drpg-window-trial [data-drpg-mode-action="openDebate"]` and press it.

findings.title: Show summary is greyed with no reason before the verdict and through a Final Trial
findings.what_happens: The button stands in the footer from the trial's start, disabled until the verdict is given, and disabled for the whole of a Final Trial, which has no summary (Q-E99-5 in the source's note). It carries no title, and no line of the console says why; the other disabled button with a cause of its own, Start the Final Trial, carries its reason as a title (:1487), and The vote's disabled state is told by the lead line.
findings.evidence:
trial-floor-ui.mjs:1453                 { action: "caseSummary", label: game.i18n.localize(progress.summaryShown ? "DRPG.CaseSummary.shown" : "DRPG.CaseSummary.show"),
trial-floor-ui.mjs:1454                   disabled: !progress.verdictApplied || Boolean(finalNow) || Boolean(progress.summaryShown), default: isDefault("caseSummary") },
findings.failure_scenario: A GM in a Final Trial after its verdict looks for the summary, finds Show summary greyed and nothing that says a Final Trial has none.
findings.expected: A title on the disabled button (after the verdict; not in a Final Trial), or the button left out of a Final Trial's footer.
findings.refutation_tried: footerButtons and dressFooter write a title only from a button's `tooltip` (ui-kit.mjs:187, 296); this spec names none. Once sent, the label itself says 'Summary sent', which is a reason. The lead line after an ordinary verdict names the summary as the next step; before the verdict and in a Final Trial it does not speak of it.
findings.probe: Open the console in a running trial before its vote and read `button[data-action="caseSummary"]`: disabled, title empty.

findings.title: Enter on a focused button of the console does nothing while any mode but the debate runs
findings.what_happens: To keep Enter from pressing the footer's default in an exchange, the console stops every Enter keydown in the capture phase on the window's root while exchangeRuns() holds, and that is any floor whose mode is not the debate: an Objection, a Rebuttal, a round, the Closing, a zone mode. The stop is not held to the footer's default, so a GM who reaches the bar's Skip, Overrule or +30 s by Tab and presses Enter moves nothing and is told nothing; Space still presses.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM working the console from the keyboard tabs to Skip during an Objection and presses Enter: the Objection runs on.
findings.expected: Enter held for the window's default alone, and a focused button pressed by it as by Space.
findings.refutation_tried: Tier 2's 'the console holds Enter while an Objection runs...' sends the key to a button and reads defaultPrevented as right, so the hold on every element is what the test pins; the note at :1777-1779 speaks of the footer's default only. Not established here: that a browser gives a button no press once its Enter keydown is prevented (not run; jsdom presses nothing on a key either way).
findings.probe: In a browser, with an Objection running and the console open, focus `[data-drpg-bar="plus"]` and press Enter, then Space; read the floor's startedAt after each.

findings.title: Move up on the first row of a round's order looks pressable and moves nothing
findings.what_happens: Every row of the order carries the same Move up button. The listener moves a row above the one before it, and for the first row there is none, so the press does nothing and nothing says so; the button is neither left out nor greyed there, and a row moved to the top keeps its button as it was.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM presses Move up on the first speaker of a Testimony's order and nothing changes.
findings.expected: The first row's button greyed or not drawn.
findings.refutation_tried: The window's render hook is the only wiring of [data-drpg-round-up] (git grep); no test or scenario presses it or Draw a new order.
findings.probe: `game.drpg.manageClassTrial()`, press the picker's Testimony, then `.drpg-round-order li:first-child [data-drpg-round-up]`; read the order of `li[data-drpg-round-id]` before and after.

not_established: Foundry v14's DialogV2 under a footer redrawn in place (ui-kit.mjs liveFooter: a button drawn later answers through options.buttons): the kit's own note leaves it to a table, LIVE-E47-01. The console and the vote window lean on it for every button drawn after the first render (The verdict, Finish the verdict, End the chapter, Send another ballot). A press of each at a table after a redraw settles it.

Whether layout clips a control at a short or narrow screen in either theme (the bar pinned under the read-out, the footer's rows, a tile's tick and start in the schema's gutter): only rules that hide were searched (display: none, visibility: hidden, pointer-events: none); the sweeps and LIVE-E70-01, LIVE-E73-05, LIVE-E99-01 are the readings, and none was run in this pass.

Close Debate posts its card without reading whether the floor closed: closeDebate (trial-floor-ui.mjs:498-509) awaits endFloor, which answers null whatever came of it (trial-floor.mjs:1356-1361). On the primary the step cannot refuse; on another GM a trial.gm that timed out or was refused would leave the debate open under a card saying it closed. Not shown here: it needs a second GM's request held or dropped (scenario 61's or 63's hold on the bridge).

A footer action that throws leaves the console closed: manageClassTrial awaits TRIAL_ACTIONS[action]() with no catch (trial-floor-ui.mjs:1826-1829), and the footer's press has already closed the window. No throwing road was found in the handlers read; the windows they open in other files (the verdict, the case summary, End of chapter, the Hall zones, the Findings) were not read to their ends in this pass.

The handlers behind the console's buttons that live in other files were traced to their first refusal and no further: verdict.mjs openVerdictDialog and openFinalVerdictDialog, case-summary.mjs showCaseSummary and replayCaseSummary, chapter.mjs openChapterEndDialog, trial-zones-ui.mjs openZonePicker and openFindings, mastermind.mjs toggleFinalTrialFlag. Their own controls are other readers' rows.
docs/dev/e59/WINDOWS.md has no row for trial-prompt.mjs promptThesis (the Scrum speaker's 'Your thesis', drpgWindow at :108), so the list of 162 windows is at least one short for these files.

The Objection's road with a voice Room on the primary GM (trial-speakers.mjs objectionTarget) was read, not pressed: no LiveKit runs headless (LIVE-E79-22). trial-speakers.mjs holds no control of its own.

Finding 6's missing redraw rests on a negative: no write of a Reveal that the console's watch hears was found in revealInStep and the functions it calls; a write deeper in those calls was not excluded. The probe in the finding settles it.

Finding 4 rests on Foundry making a Setting document on a setting's first write (createSetting, then updateSetting), stated by the module's own notes and not read from Foundry's source in this pass; and on a world reaching its first trial without that document, which depends on the world.
